title: Surgical circuit-quarantine + on-call cookbook for progressive traffic shedding
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create an operational pattern and automation that enables engineers and on-call responders to perform 'surgical quarantine' of failing circuits and apply progressive, policy-driven traffic shedding across regions with minimal noisy paging. Deliverables: (1) a standardized on-call cookbook with clear decision trees and automated actions, (2) orchestration knobs for circuit quarantine and stepwise shedding, (3) alert-filtering rules and telemetry signatures to reduce low-signal pages, and (4) integration tests + runbook drills.
background: We have recurrent incidents where noisy low-signal alerts cause on-call fatigue during partial regional degradations. Existing shedding is coarse (global or service-wide) and rollback is manual. Multi-region failover sometimes triggers unnecessary model fallbacks and capacity thrashing. We need a reproducible, low-noise way to isolate degraded serving circuits, shed nonessential traffic progressively, and automate routine remediations while keeping humans in the decision loop for high-impact actions.
goal: Reduce noisy paging by 60% for region-specific SLO degradations, shorten time-to-safe-state via automated circuit quarantine and staged shedding, and provide a clear cookbook that on-call can follow during a degradation resulting from kernel queue saturation, memory pressure, or network partial outage.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc published and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and Product (sign-off from at least 3 reviewers)
Automation playbook able to quarantine a single serving circuit and apply tiered shedding policy without manual intervention in a controlled blackout test
Alert volume reduction: synthetic partial-region degradation test yields >=60% fewer noisy pages to on-call compared to baseline
Metrics exposed: per-circuit error_rate, queue_depth, shed_level, and quarantine_state are visible in Console dashboards
Automated canary failsafe: system automatically rolls back shedding if error_rate improves to within SLO within configured hysteresis window
runbook_steps: Step 0: Ingest alert. Use the incident triage GUI to attach telemetry fingerprints. If alert is 'low-signal' and matches known noisy signature, auto-suppress for 10 minutes and create a suppressed incident (no page).

Step 1: If alert indicates 'circuit degradation' (queue_depth > 90th percentile and token_latency spike), check cross-region error divergence. If divergence < 10% then mark as local; otherwise escalate to multi-region flag.

Step 2: Execute 'surgical quarantine' on affected circuit: set quarantine_state=isolated which gates incoming new sessions for that circuit. Monitor shed_level and downstream error_rate for 2 minutes.

Step 3: Apply progressive shedding tiers: TIER-1 (non-critical routes: embeddings bulk, analytics) -> TIER-2 (low-priority generation models) -> TIER-3 (throttled sampling for interactive gen). Each tier applied when queue_depth or GPU_util exceeds thresholds. Wait 60s between tiers for stabilization.

Step 4: If cross-region failover is required, route traffic to healthy region(s) using policy 'prefer-local-with-latency-boundary' to avoid global cascading. Trigger canary traffic first (1%) for 30s then scale incrementally.
Step 5: If quarantined circuit recovers within hysteresis window (configurable, default 5m), automatically lift quarantine and run reconciliation to flush any prefix caches safely.
Step 6: If recovery fails after predefined window (default 20m), escalate to oncall L2 and kick off capacity rebalancing workflow and model-variant fallback (if configured).
playbooks: Noise-filter playbook: telemetry signatures for known noisy alerts (e.g., synthetic canary misfires, transient infra flaps) and adaptive suppression rules
Surgical Quarantine playbook: circuit identification, isolation API call sequence, and post-quarantine reconciliation checklist
Progressive Shedding playbook: predefined tiers, mapping of routes to tiers, and rollback conditions
Cross-region failover playbook: canary routing, cost-aware shift, and SLA-aware repeatable checks
Escalation playbook: when to involve runtime/infra/product and how to log customer-impact and RCA tracing anchors
dashboards: Console: 'Circuit Health' - per-cluster/circuit KPIs with quarantine overlays (https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/circuit-health)
Console: 'Shedding & Pages' - mapping of active shed_level to ongoing paging activity (https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/shedding-pages)
Grafana: 'Regional Divergence' - top-level SLO deltas by region (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/regions/divergence)

notes: We should avoid hard-coded thresholds; expose per-service percentile baselines for adaptive thresholds.
Consider adding a 'silent-failover' mode where traffic is shifted without audible pages for first-line suppression during business hours.
Customer-impact labeling must be part of every automated step to ensure compliance and proper billing/logging.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overaggressive suppression might hide an emerging large-scale outage. Mitigation: require a 'meta-alert' that monitors suppressed incidents and pages if suppressed incident count exceeds threshold.
Risk: Quarantine may create cache cold starts and increase latencies elsewhere. Mitigation: perform warmed canary and gradual ramp to detect adverse effects early.
Risk: Incorrect tier mapping could shed essential traffic. Mitigation: maintain an explicit route->tier manifest and require PM approval for changes to tier assignments.
